idea-plugin.name: Editor Browser
idea-plugin.description:
Websites as editor tabs, right next to your files.

  • One tab per site: Tools › Open URL in Editor Tab… opens localhost:3000, backend.test/admin or any address as a normal editor tab; Tools › New Browser Tab opens a blank one to type into.
  • Splits like a file: right-click the tab › Split Right for code and site side by side.
  • Back, forward, reload, an address bar, zoom (handy in a narrow split) and DevTools in every tab; the page's own favicon becomes the tab icon.
  • Device widths: see the page at a phone, tablet or laptop width, centred in the tab.
  • Light / dark mode: check a site's dark mode (prefers-color-scheme) per tab, without switching your OS.
  • Clear site data: the page's cookies, storage and cache gone in one click, for a fresh first visit.
  • Password-protected sites (HTTP basic auth, e.g. a staging server) ask for a login in a Sign In dialog, optionally remembered in the IDE's password store.
  • Saving a project file reloads the tabs on a local page (localhost, *.test, …); pages with their own hot reload (Vite, webpack) are left to it for front-end files.
  • Find in page (⌘F), and a toolbar badge counting the page's console errors.
  • You see what a page is doing: a progress line and a spinning tab icon while it loads, a bar saying why a page didn't load (with Try Again), a 404 / 500 badge, and a tab that reloads by itself once its local dev server is up.
  • A toolbar you arrange: put each optional button on the toolbar, in its ⋮ menu or hide it.
  • Share preview: the link card a page gets in Slack, X, LinkedIn or WhatsApp (its og: / twitter: meta tags), in a popover, with what is missing.
  • Links that open a new window (target="_blank") open as a new tab.
  • Tabs come back after a restart on the page you left them; logins are shared by all tabs.
  • Right-click a selected URL in code › Open in Editor Tab.
  • Right-click an HTML file › Open In › Browser Tab shows it as a page, straight from disk.
  • PDF files open as an editor tab in Chromium's PDF viewer (thumbnails, zoom, find, print) instead of the system's PDF app, and reload when they change on disk; toggle under Settings › Tools › Editor Browser.
  • Starting a dev server opens it as a tab automatically, both from a run configuration (its printed localhost URL) and from the Terminal (npm run dev, php -S, … on a common dev-server port such as 5173, 3000 or 8000); toggle this under Settings › Tools › Editor Browser.

Uses PhpStorm's own embedded Chromium (JCEF). Free and open source on GitHub.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.7.0

  • PDF files open in a browser tab: double-click a PDF in the project (or open it any other way) and it shows as an editor tab in Chromium's PDF viewer, with page thumbnails, zoom, rotate, print and download, instead of in the system's PDF app. On by default; Settings › Tools › Editor Browser › Open PDF files in a browser tab. The tab is the PDF file itself: it splits, and comes back after a restart, like any file.
  • A PDF tab reloads when its file changes on disk, e.g. a report or invoice you generate again.
  • Find in page (⌘F) works in a PDF: it highlights the matches and steps through them. It shows no match count there (the viewer doesn't report one) rather than "No matches".
  • On a PDF the tab's zoom buttons and ⌘+ / ⌘− are off (they didn't change the PDF): the viewer's own − / + zoom it.
  • Open In › Browser Tab also for PDF files.

0.6.0

  • Loading is visible: a progress line under the toolbar and a spinning tab icon while a page loads, and Reload turns into Stop (✕) only then (before, the spinning reload icon was a Stop button, so clicking "refresh" on a slow page cancelled it). A double click on Reload no longer stops the load it started.
  • A server that hasn't answered after 3 s gets a "Waiting for localhost:8000" bar (paused at a breakpoint?), with Stop.
  • A page that can't load gets a red bar saying why, in words (nothing running on that port, unknown host, connection closed, certificate, redirect loop, …), with Try Again, and a red tab icon.
  • A local server that refused the connection (a dev server still starting): the tab waits for it and reloads by itself once it accepts connections; Stop Waiting turns that off.
  • An HTTP error answer shows as a 404 / 500 badge in the toolbar (a 5xx also turns the tab icon red); a crashed page gets a bar with Reload.

0.5.0

  • Light / dark mode: ⋮ › Color Scheme › Light or Dark makes the page see that prefers-color-scheme, to check a site's dark mode without switching your OS; per tab, kept after a restart. A "Dark" label in the toolbar goes back to the system's.
  • Clear Site Data (⋮): deletes the page's cookies and storage (local / session storage, IndexedDB, service workers, Cache Storage), empties the browser cache and reloads.
  • HTTP basic auth: a site that asks for a username and password (e.g. a staging server) gets a Sign In dialog; the login is used for that site until the IDE restarts, or remembered in the IDE's password store. Digest authentication isn't supported.
  • Fix: pages that set their background on body (e.g. dark sites) showed a white body; the page's own background now wins, pages without one are white, and pages in a dark color scheme get Chromium's dark canvas.

0.4.0

  • Share Preview: shows the link card the page gets when its URL is pasted into Slack, X, LinkedIn or WhatsApp (its og: / twitter: meta tags: image, site, title, description) in a popover, with what is missing or too long: no og:image, a relative image URL, an image under 600 × 315 px, a title past 60 characters, …
  • A calmer toolbar: back / forward / reload, the address bar, New Tab and DevTools, plus a ⋮ menu with device width, zoom, find, share preview and open in default browser. Settings › Tools › Editor Browser (or ⋮ › Customize Toolbar…) puts each item on the toolbar, in ⋮ or hides it; shortcuts keep working for hidden items.

0.3.1

  • The reload button spins for at least half a second after a reload, so a page that reloads in a few milliseconds (a local dev server, reload on save) visibly reloaded; the spin follows the icon's arrows.

0.3.0

  • Device widths: a toolbar button lays the page out at a phone (390 px), tablet (768 px) or laptop (1280 px) width, centred in the tab, to check its responsive layout; remembered per tab.
  • Open In › Browser Tab: an HTML file of the project as a page (from the project view, the editor, its tab or the HTML editor's floating browser bar); running it again reuses the tab.
  • Reload on save: saving a project file reloads the tabs on a local page (a tab in the background when you switch to it). Pages whose dev server reloads them itself (Vite, webpack HMR, LiveReload, Browsersync) only reload for server-side files such as PHP, Twig or Blade. Toggle under Settings › Tools › Editor Browser.
  • Find in page: ⌘F (Ctrl+F) opens a find bar with the number of matches; Enter, ⌘G / ⇧⌘G or F3 step through them.
  • A red badge in the toolbar counts the page's console errors; hover for the messages, click for DevTools.

0.2.2

  • Right-click › View Page Source works: it opens the page's HTML in a new tab (it did nothing before), and that tab reopens as source after a restart.

0.2.1

  • A globe button in the main toolbar opens a New Browser Tab in one click.
  • Dev servers started in the Terminal open as a tab too: a common dev-server port (5173, 3000, 8000, 8080, …) starting to listen is noticed within a couple of seconds.
  • Restarting a dev server reloads its tab; 127.0.0.1 and localhost count as the same server.
  • The shortcuts are ⌥⇧⌘T / ⌥⇧⌘U on macOS (the docs said ⌃⌥⇧).

0.2.0

  • New Browser Tab: a blank tab with the address bar focused, from the Tools menu, a tab's right-click menu, a toolbar button, or ⌥⇧⌘T (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+T on Windows / Linux).
  • The page's own favicon becomes the tab icon.
  • A run configuration printing a localhost URL opens it as a tab automatically (reusing the tab on a restart); toggle under Settings › Tools › Editor Browser.

0.1.0

  • First release: browser tabs in the editor, address bar, back / forward / reload, zoom, DevTools, new-window links as tabs, tabs restored after a restart.
